answer.evidence: Rows 2-8 form a light tan top band, 7 rows deep. It ends in a lighter front-edge line at row 8 (#ddbf91), followed by darker shadow rows 9-10 (#8a6128, then #a67a37). styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a one-tile wooden wine rack with a light wood frame, a 4x4 grid of dark cubbies and small red bottle ends. Measured facts support the look. It has 16 visible tones per tile against 17 for the cheese stall, 20 for the well and 9 for the hedge, so it sits within the reference range. Near-flat coverage is 0%, and 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines lean brown rather than black. The frame shows several wood steps (highlight, light, mid, dark, deep cubby shadow). The bottles carry 2-3 tones each, with a highlight on each bottle end. No large flat fills are visible. Its total of 17 distinct colours is lower than the 38-40 of the richer references, but most of those are near-identical shades. It is slightly simpler than the stall and well, yet a careful artist would accept it next to the bench and hedge without it looking like a sticker.
